svg.title: Figure 2. Eccentric load in a plane of symmetry, and the kern
svg.desc: Two panels. (a) Stress across the depth of a rectangular section loaded at a quarter of the depth above the centroid: a uniform block P over A plus a linear bending distribution, minus M z y over I z, gives a combined distribution that is tension over most of the depth and compression near the bottom; the neutral axis, where the combined stress is zero, lies below the centroid, on the side away from the load. (b) A rectangle with its kern, a diamond whose half-diagonals are h over 6 along y and b over 6 along z. Three load points on the y axis are shown with their neutral axes: a load inside the kern puts the neutral axis outside the section, a load on the kern boundary puts it exactly on the bottom edge, and a load outside the kern brings it into the section. The farther the load moves out, the closer the neutral axis comes to the centroid.
